conflicts.point: Whether structural separation of chip manufacturing, cloud hosting, and model development introduces prohibitive coordination friction and latency penalties for frontier AI training clusters.

positions.stance: Argues that unbundling chip design, cloud infrastructure, and model training creates multi-year coordination delays and communication latencies that halt capability scaling.
Maintains that unbundling infrastructure from service providers does not disrupt technical execution, pointing to historical precedents like the 1982 AT&T divestiture.

verdicts.conflict: Whether structural separation of chip manufacturing, cloud hosting, and model development introduces prohibitive coordination friction and latency penalties for frontier AI training clusters.
verdicts.rationale: Both camps rely on conflicting structural analogies rather than direct empirical measurements of frontier AI training workloads. The safetyists cite historical telecommunications divestitures, while the accelerationists point to modern data center energy constraints and grid connection queues. Neither side provides definitive performance data from unbundled AI infrastructure clusters of equivalent scale.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Benchmarking data from distributed training runs across independent cloud providers that measures exact inter-node communication latency penalties compared to vertically integrated clusters would tip the balance.
